requirements.title: PAD values are YES, or NO
requirements.definition: The scalar default character expression in a PAD= specifier shall evaluate to YES, or NO.

pending.pad-yes-value: Positive source/control uses PAD="YES" in a context admitted by 12.6.2.1; trailing blanks/case-insensitivity remain covered by 12.6.2.1 p4.
pending.pad-no-value: Positive source/control uses PAD="NO" in a context admitted by 12.6.2.1; trailing blanks/case-insensitivity remain covered by 12.6.2.1 p4.
pending.pad-other-value-source-control: Source-control negative changes only the PAD= value to an unlisted token such as "MAYBE"; no numbered diagnostic is claimed for this unnumbered value rule.

requirements.oracle: Plans are pending and source-derived. Positive plans establish a non-default state first (for example by writing known records, initializing variables to nonzero/nonblank sentinels, or using a compile-only conforming control) and then observe only portable properties: exact internal records, successful IOSTAT zero, nonzero IOSTAT or named status values where the standard names them, required INQUIRE tokens, or required diagnosis of a numbered syntax rule or constraint. Negative/source-control plans change one property from the conforming control and do not require a particular diagnostic message, severity, exit status, or printed rule number.

requirements.title: PAD temporarily changes the connection pad mode
requirements.definition: The PAD= specifier temporarily changes the pad mode for the connection.

pending.pad-temporary-change: Use formatted input from an external short record on a connection opened PAD="NO" and statement PAD="YES"; initialize the target to -777 and expect the padded read result fixed by 12.6.4.5.3, then INQUIRE(PAD=; 12.10.2.21) sentinel reports NO. Use the dual statement PAD="NO" with a short record and initialized IOSTAT/SIZE targets; assert only the portable no-padding status/effect fixed by 12.6.4.5.3 and restore via INQUIRE(PAD=; 12.10.2.21) to YES.
pending.pad-mode-restored-after-statement: The temporary-change plans explicitly pre-establish a nondefault connection mode with OPEN, perform one data transfer with a different statement specifier, and use post-transfer INQUIRE with a nonmatching sentinel to assert restoration rather than merely successful transfer.

requirements.title: Omitted PAD leaves the connection pad mode unchanged
requirements.definition: If the PAD= specifier is omitted, the pad mode is not changed.

pending.omitted-pad-does-not-change-mode: Open with PAD="NO", omit PAD= on a formatted READ, prefill INQUIRE variable with a sentinel, and expect INQUIRE(PAD=; 12.10.2.21) to remain NO.

accounting.rationale: Single paragraph mixes PAD= value restriction, temporary mode effect/restoration, and omitted-specifier no-change rule.

review_rationale: Source registration for 12.6.2.2-12.6.2.16, the individual io-control-spec specifiers (batch160). Every unit hash-verified by independent reviewers across two rounds. Each temporary mode specifier is split into its value restriction, its one-statement effect with restoration of the connection mode (observed by INQUIRE after the statement), and the omitted-means-unchanged rule. Round 1 found a pending plan expecting exact output from I2 on a positive value without fixing the sign mode; it now uses SS, and a sweep found no other plus-, leading-zero- or rounding-dependent exact output. R1215 and C1232 were pre-accounted. Source accounting only.
